title: C4046A — Left-hand license plate lamp connector
introduction:
I read this reference from identity to cavity to circuit. Start with CNumber and Description in the identification table, then use the printed cavity labels in the drawing to find the matching Cavity row below. Think of those labels as addresses: the connector outline helps you recognize the layout, while the table tells you what belongs at each address.

Read across the whole pin-assignment row to connect its circuit identifier, wire description, function and terminal reference. The ground entry describes the current-return path; the park-lamp relay entry identifies the relay-related circuit. A relay is an electrically controlled switch, but that label alone does not promise a separate plug-in relay.

This page explains identification and the circuit map. It does not teach access, probing, testing or replacement. The drawing's physical viewing side, the gauge convention and the meanings of Size and Used are unspecified here; retain those entries as reference data without assigning extra meanings. A COMPLETE status describes the reference record, not the electrical health of the connection.

edits.why: I use the rounded housing outline and the rectangular feature on the drawing's right to keep the illustration visually aligned while reading its cavity labels. These are landmarks within the drawing, not instructions for holding or approaching the installed connector. The identification row beneath it associates the illustrated face with the listed shell and harness.

The Cavity column is the bridge between the drawing and each electrical entry. Circuit Number identifies the circuit; Function explains its assigned role. Reading those together avoids treating wire color alone as an identity check. A ground or relay label describes a connection's purpose, not a test result or proof that current can pass.

A pigtail is a connector with attached wire leads. I keep its service-part record separate from the harness pin assignments: their Gauge entries describe their respective records, not an instruction to choose replacement wire. Service Part and Engineering Shell identify different aspects of the listed item; this lookup does not teach terminal removal or splicing.
